-- Converted: CREATE JOIN INDEX sales.jix_order AS SELECT ... -> CREATE VIEW SALES.JIX_ORDER with the same SELECT, fully qualified names.
-- Reason: Snowflake has no join indexes and its materialized views cannot contain joins; a view keeps the same name and result set.
CREATE VIEW SALES.JIX_ORDER AS
SELECT h.ORDER_ID, l.PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES.ORDER_HEADER h
JOIN SALES.ORDER_LINE l ON h.ORDER_ID = l.ORDER_ID;

unsupported: Join index materialization and automatic optimizer use: the view is computed at query time and is not stored or maintained.

assumptions: Executed with SnowSQL using a named connection configured for key-pair authentication; the masked .LOGON credentials are not reproduced.

The export is meant to be CSV (inferred from the .csv file name); BTEQ's default export record format is not reproduced byte-for-byte, and SnowSQL's CSV output includes a header row by default (add !set header=false if the consumer expects none).
/tmp is writable on the machine running SnowSQL.
explanations: BTEQ client script converted to a SnowSQL script; every BTEQ dot-command maps to a SnowSQL ! command, and the query keeps the same columns.
The naming-map entry "ZIP/LOAD_SCRIPT".SQL is a file path, not a database object, so it is used only as the output file name.

-- Converted: .LOGON ***MASKED*** -> removed; connect with: snowsql -c <named_connection> -f load_script.sql
-- Reason: SnowSQL takes credentials from the connection config (key-pair authentication for service users), never inline in the script (rule snowflake.security.no_plaintext_credentials).

-- Converted: .SET QUIET ON -> !set quiet=true (plus timing/friendly off so only results are written).
-- Reason: SnowSQL client option equivalent of BTEQ quiet mode.
!set quiet=true
!set timing=false
!set friendly=false

-- Converted: .EXPORT FILE = /tmp/customer.csv -> !set output_format=csv + !spool /tmp/customer.csv
-- Reason: SnowSQL writes query output to a local file with !spool; output_format=csv matches the .csv target file.
!set output_format=csv
!spool /tmp/customer.csv

-- Converted: SEL -> SELECT; sales.customer -> SALES.CUSTOMER.
-- Reason: SEL is a Teradata-only abbreviation; object name taken from the naming map.
SELECT CUSTOMER_ID, CUSTOMER_NAME FROM SALES.CUSTOMER;

-- Converted: .EXPORT RESET -> !spool off
-- Reason: Stops writing output to the export file.
!spool off

-- Converted: .LOGOFF -> !exit
-- Reason: Ends the SnowSQL session.
!exit

unsupported: Exact BTEQ .EXPORT record format (DATA/REPORT mode layout) has no SnowSQL equivalent; output is CSV.

-- Converted: CREATE PROCEDURE (IN p_account BIGINT, IN p_amount DECIMAL(12, 2)) LANGUAGE SQL DYNAMIC RESULT SETS 1 SQL SECURITY OWNER -> Snowflake Scripting procedure with RETURNS VARCHAR, EXECUTE AS OWNER and a $$-delimited body; IN keywords and DYNAMIC RESULT SETS 1 removed.
-- Reason: Snowflake requires RETURNS and a delimited body, has no IN parameter mode keyword, maps SQL SECURITY OWNER to EXECUTE AS OWNER (rule snowflake.rule.procedure_execute_as), and the source never opens a result-set cursor so DYNAMIC RESULT SETS has no effect.
CREATE PROCEDURE SALES.ADD_PAYMENT(P_ACCOUNT BIGINT, P_AMOUNT DECIMAL(12, 2))
RETURNS VARCHAR
LANGUAGE SQL
EXECUTE AS OWNER
AS
$$
BEGIN
  -- Converted: parameters referenced as :P_ACCOUNT / :P_AMOUNT; table name mapped to SALES.PAYMENT.
  -- Reason: Snowflake Scripting binds variables inside SQL statements with a colon prefix.
  INSERT INTO SALES.PAYMENT (PAYMENT_ID, ACCOUNT_ID, AMOUNT) VALUES (1, :P_ACCOUNT, :P_AMOUNT);
  -- Converted: table name mapped to SALES.AUDIT_LOG; statement otherwise unchanged.
  -- Reason: Naming map.
  INSERT INTO SALES.AUDIT_LOG (EVENT_ID, EVENT_TYPE) VALUES (1, 'PAYMENT');
  -- Converted: added RETURN NULL.
  -- Reason: Snowflake procedures must declare a return type; the source returns nothing.
  RETURN NULL;
END;
$$;
